log.msg: CENSUS: 133 pages listed, 133 probed, 133 measured (0 failed). At 1280 the first heading sits at TEN different distances from the region edge — 0, 15, 20, 30, 42, 51, 62, 269, 387, 401px — and EIGHT different kinds of box pay it: a page grid TRACK (73 pages), ext/Doc's .doc-well (52), Page.css's region-default padding (3), the v3 board's own head (1), the columns host's --page-column-pad-x (1), layouts' std-shell rail (1), the resume's own head (1), and on /framework/ai2/ nothing at all (ink at 0px).

VIOLATIONS: 19 of 133 pages put ink closer than one rung (--gap-25, the smallest step the size standard has) to the region edge at at least one of 400/1280/1920/3440. It gets WORSE as the screen gets wider: 3 pages at 1280, 8 at 1920, 7 at 3440. /framework/ext/Panel/ is NEGATIVE at three widths (-28, -29, -3) — ink past the edge.

THE CAUSE OF THE WIDE-SCREEN CLIFF, named: ext/toc/toc.css's `.page:has(> .toc)` replaces the page's whole grid-template-columns with `minmax(0, 1fr) 15rem` above 82em. That template has NO gutter tracks, so every page that calls toc() loses BOTH gutters at exactly 1312px and up — its title lands at x=0 against the sidebar. That is the owner's verbatim complaint ('I just clicked on framework/styles and the text is butting up against the sidebar with zero pixels of padding') and it is why /framework/styles/, /framework/core/, /framework/versus/ and /framework/faq/ measure 42px at 1280 and 0px at 1920. `.page:has(> .page-related)` in Page.css rewrites the same template and keeps its gutters, which is why the bug is in one file, not two. padding-law owns toc.css; I have not touched it.

THE SHEETS: 40 rules in 25 live stylesheets set a page-level inset. ONE gives the gutter (Page.css `.page`); 19 take it away (`--gutter-x: 0px` or `padding: 0` on a page box — .page.full, .page.columns, .page.topic, .page.doc-page, .page-section .page, three :has() board overrides, .page.blogx x2, .page.shell x2, .page.blog-part, .page.std-shell, .page.scene-note and more); 8 pay it back by hand (`padding-inline: var(--gutter-x)` on a wall, a bleed grid, a demo stage, a layout, a notes shot). A gutter given once, removed nineteen times and refunded eight times is the whole shape of the problem.

decision.question: What counts as 'the edge the text must not touch' for a site whose pages nest inside topic shells with their own sidebars?
options: the innermost region (.pages) that holds content
decision.chose: the innermost region (.pages) that holds content
decision.why: That box's inline-start edge IS the rail's edge on a page with a sidebar and the window's edge on one without — one number covers every shell, which is what makes the 133 pages comparable. Keying off the page instead measured the topic SHELL, sidebar included, and read a false 0px on /blog/ and /framework/.

decision.question: Is the fix one rule, and should it be applied?
options: gutter as PADDING on the page, bleed as the child's opt-out (Page.css)
gutter as padding on the REGION (.pages) so no page rule can touch it
write it as a brief and apply nothing
decision.chose: gutter as PADDING on the page, bleed as the child's opt-out
decision.why: It is one model, three declarations, one file, and it removes the whole class of failure the owner hit: a rule that rewrites grid-template-columns can no longer reach the inset. Measured over 133 pages at four widths, violating pages went 6 to 1, only 7 pages moved at all, and no page gained a sideways scrollbar. The region alternative is stronger — nothing on the page could zero it — but it makes `bleed` impossible, and the homepage bands, the blog hero and every /imagine/ realm depend on a page reaching the window edge; that cost is larger than the bug. Applying nothing was the third option and was rejected because the model was already proved in the worktree, which is what a worktree is for.

log.msg: APPLIED in the worktree, core/Page/Page.css only: (1) `.page` grid-template-columns loses its two gutter tracks and `padding` gains `var(--gutter-x)`; (2) `.page > .bleed` gains `margin-inline: calc(var(--gutter-x) * -1)`; (3) `.page` gains `--page-pad: initial`; (4) the `:has(> .page-related)` template loses its gutters and takes a `column-gap` instead, or it would have paid the outer inset twice on every page that says `related:`. OVERRIDE LINES RETIRED: NONE, on purpose — the eight `padding-inline: var(--gutter-x)` payback rules in six sheets still work unchanged because a bleed still reaches the edge, so this lands without touching another stylesheet. Retiring them means deciding a card wall should stop bleeding by default, which is a separate change.

PROOF, 133 pages x 400/1280/1920/3440, before and after: pages with ink closer than one rung to the region edge went 6 -> 1. Fixed: /framework/styles/, /core/, /versus/, /faq/, /start/ — all 0px at 1920 and 3440 before, 67px and 90px after. The one left is /framework/ai2/, a `.page.full` that zeroes its own gutter. Only 7 of 133 pages moved at all; the document scrolls sideways on 0 pages before and after; one new overflow appeared (a code block on /framework/ux/Tree/ at 3440). /resume/ lost 28px of inset at 400 (42 -> 14) and stays far from the edge.

THE ONE KNOWN COST, measured: a `bleed` child lands 3px short at 1280 and 5px at 1920. `--gutter-x` is a clamp holding a PERCENTAGE, and a percentage in a child's margin resolves against the child's containing block — the page's content box, two gutters narrower — so the negative margin is 4% of a smaller number than the padding was (4% of 955.9 = 38.2 against 4% of 1039 = 41.6). Page.css already writes this trap down for the columns host ('cqi, never %'). Removing it means changing the gutter's own formula, which is the owner's call; @property cannot rescue it because a `<length>` syntax rejects a clamp containing a percentage.

MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, before the numbers above: the first census measured ink against the nearest horizontally-SCROLLED ancestor rather than the region, which reported /framework/styles/system/ as 1px when every paragraph on it sits at 28 — it was reading a code block's own padding. Skipping ink inside a real horizontal scroller (the layout skill's own exclude list) took the 400px violation count from 15 to 1 and the any-width count from 19 to 6. The 19-page figure in my earlier log line is wrong; 6 is the real number. Resize-vs-fresh-load was checked on five pages x two widths and agreed on nine of ten.

assign.outcome:
**The gutter is padding on the page now, not two empty grid columns — and five top-level pages stopped touching the sidebar.**

A page's inset used to be a column of empty grid on each side of the text. That meant any rule replacing `grid-template-columns` deleted the whole inset, silently: `ext/toc` does exactly that above 1312px, which is why /framework/styles/, /core/, /versus/, /faq/ and /start/ looked right on a laptop and put their title hard against the sidebar on a wide screen. The inset is now padding on the page, which no template can reach, and a `bleed` child is the only way out of it.

[The analysis](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/layout-analysis/) — the before/after picture, four real pages drawn at actual size showing where every pixel of their padding comes from, five plain sentences on why it keeps going wrong, and the rule.
[The counts](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/layout-analysis/counts/) — 133 pages listed, 133 measured, at 400/1280/1920/3440: the violations, the ten different insets at one width, the eight kinds of box that pay them, the 38 rules, and how it was measured.

![before and after](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/layout-analysis/shots/styles-1920-after.png)

**What the numbers say.** Ten different insets on 133 pages at one single width. One rule in the whole site gives a page its gutter, 18 take it away and 8 hand it back by name. Pages with text closer to the region edge than one rung went from **6 to 1** after the change, and the one left is /framework/ai2/, a `.page.full` that zeroes its own gutter on purpose. Seven pages moved at all; none gained a sideways scrollbar.

**What I deliberately left.**
- **No overrides deleted.** The eight `padding-inline: var(--gutter-x)` payback rules still work unchanged, so this landed without touching another stylesheet. Retiring them means deciding a card wall should stop bleeding by default — a separate change.
- **One known cost:** a `bleed` child lands 3px short at 1280 and 5px at 1920, because `--gutter-x` is a clamp holding a percentage and a percentage re-resolves against the child's own box. Fixing it means changing the gutter's formula, which is the owner's call.
- **Four doc lines still describe grid tracks** (styles/doc/layout-system.md:11-22, core/Page/readme.md:33, core/Page/doc/columns.md:477, doc/decisions.md:298) — outside my fence, one edit each, spelled out in the log.
- **padding-law must not also restore the gutter in toc.css** — the cause is fixed one level up, and doing both gives those five pages double padding.
